claim: Thames Path Henley to Marlow is 8.7 miles (14 km) passing Temple Island, Hambleden Lock and Mill, Hurley and Bisham Church; Marlow to Windsor is 14.3 miles via Bourne End, Cookham, Cliveden Reach and Boulter's Lock.
quote: Day 1: Henley-on-Thames to Marlow Distance: 8.7 miles / 14 km ... Hambleden Lock ... Day 2: Marlow to Windsor Distance: 14.3 miles / 23 km ... Cookham ... Boulter's Lock ... Cliveden Estate

claim: The Henley to Marlow section is described as one of the most scenic and quintessentially English stretches of the Thames Path, with gentle level paths and Hambleden Lock reached after about 3 miles.
quote: walking downstream from Henley-on-Thames to Marlow offers riverside inns, wooden footbridges, lush meadows and postcard-perfect villages. It's a gentle walk on mainly level paths ... After around 3 miles, you reach Hambleden Lock

claim: Coombe Hill is the highest viewpoint in the Chiltern Hills at 260m (852 ft), offering panoramic views over the Aylesbury Vale and on clear days as far as the Cotswolds, on a moderately energetic circular trail past Chequers.
quote: At 260m (852 feet) above sea level, Coombe Hill is the highest viewpoint in the Chiltern Hills, affording panoramic views over the Aylesbury Vale, and on a clear day you can see as far as the Cotswolds.

claim: The Whiteleaf and Chequers Circular is the top-rated Chilterns walk (4.7 stars, 1,663 reviews on AllTrails), taking in Whiteleaf Hill Nature Reserve and the 1742-recorded chalk Whiteleaf Cross.
quote: the Whiteleaf and Chequers Circular is rated 4.7 stars from 1,663 reviews ... Whiteleaf Cross is a chalk hill figure first recorded in 1742

claim: French Brothers run Windsor public Thames cruises with a 40-minute round trip (Adult £13.50) and 2-hour round trip (Adult £22), departing daily every 30 minutes from 10am-5pm 11 February to 29 October from Windsor Promenade.
quote: 40-Minute Round Trip: Adult £13.50 ... 2-Hour Round Trip: Adult £22 ... 11 February to 29 October: Daily – every 30 minutes from 10am to 5pm

claim: Hobbs of Henley, a family-run business with over 150 years of experience and the largest fleet on the Thames, hires self-drive Pilot Class diesel boats, Pearly Class outboard launches and luxury Linssen cruisers by the hour, day or week.
quote: Pilot Class boats are practical and easy to use, built from fiberglass with a diesel inboard engine ... Luxury Linssen self-drive cruisers, the only ones for hire in the UK ... Pearly Class Launches

claim: Burnham Beeches is a National Nature Reserve, SSSI and Special Area of Conservation managed by the City of London, with a 1-mile sensory trail, 5-mile historical trail and 3 km geology trail; car parks open from 8am to dusk with daily charges.
quote: The sensory trail is the shortest at just under one mile long ... The historical trail is around five miles long and takes about 2.5 hours ... Car parks are open from 8am and close at dusk, with daily parking charges applying

claim: National Cycle Route 4 runs east-west through the Royal Borough via Egham, Windsor, Eton, Bray, Maidenhead, Cookham and on towards Henley, taking in Windsor Great Park and the Thames.
quote: NCN Route 4 (London to Reading) passes through the Royal Borough from Egham in the east, via Windsor, Eton, Bray, and Maidenhead, before heading off towards Henley in the west.

claim: Windsor Great Park covers around 1,942 hectares (4,800 acres), is open free 7am to dusk, and welcomes cyclists as part of NCN4 — but groups must be max six riders, two abreast, and cycles are banned on the Long Walk, Deer Park and Valley Gardens.
quote: Windsor Great Park is part of the operational Windsor Estate that covers around 1,942 hectares (4,800 acres) ... You should ride in groups of no more than 6, and no more than 2 abreast ... Cycles are not permitted on the Long Walk, nor in the Deer Park and Valley Gardens

claim: Paddleboard Maidenhead, established 2014, operates from Ray Mill Island with British Canoeing level 3 coaches running lessons, SUP Club sessions and Thames paddleboarding trips.
quote: A family-run business established in 2014, operating from Ray Mill Island ... British Canoeing level 3 coaches for Thames paddleboarding trips, SUP Club and lessons

claim: Moose Canoe and SUP Hire is based at Bisham Abbey near Marlow and hires Canadian canoes, sit-on-top kayaks and SUPs along the River Thames.
quote: Based at Bisham Abbey near Marlow and also operates all along the River Thames. They hire Canadian Canoes, Sit on Top Kayaks and SUPs.

claim: Henley Canoe Hire offers canoe, kayak and SUP rentals on the Thames from 1-hour up to half-day and full-day paddles with custom adventure packages.
quote: exclusive canoe, kayak, and stand-up paddleboard rentals along the River Thames ... 1-hour hire to relaxing half-day or full-day paddles, plus customized adventure packages

claim: The Cliveden estate has 375 acres of woodlands, riverbank and formal gardens with several waymarked walking trails offering views over the Thames; National Trust membership or admission fee required.
quote: Cliveden offers a varied selection of dog-friendly walking trails with 375 acres of woodlands, riverbank and formal gardens

claim: Caversham Boat Services in Reading hires self-drive day boats including the 12-person Montego, with options to cruise west towards Goring or east towards Henley and tuition provided on the day.
quote: spacious Thames day boat called the Montego, which holds up to 12 people ... cruising either west towards Goring or east towards Henley in a day

claim: The SUP Life runs a guided Henley-to-Maidenhead paddleboarding adventure passing Hambleden, Medmenham, Hurley, Marlow, Bourne End and finishing at Boulters Lock.
quote: Henley to Maidenhead trip which includes welcome breakfast, paddling through Hambleden, Medmenham and Hurley to Marlow for lunch, then to Bourne End and finishing at Boulters Lock in Maidenhead
